Reported Spill Volume: 50 gallon
Report Description////////THIS IS AN UPDATE FOR NRC REPORT NUMBER 1280352.//////// UPDATED INFO: - 40 - 50 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL DISCHARGED FROM THE SECONDARY LOCOMOTIVE. - THERE WERE NO ANHYDROUS AMMONIA TANK CARS INVOLVED. ALL FOUR DERAILED RAIL CARS WERE EMPTY PLASTIC PELLET CARS. - THE LOCOMOTIVE ONLY KNOCKED OVER ONE POWER POLE. NEARBY GRADE CROSSING EQUIPMENT WAS STRUCK AS THE TRAIN WAS MOVING WITH THE POWER POLE WEDGED AGAINST THE LOCOMOTIVE. - DAMAGE AMOUNT IS ESTIMATED TO BE $750,000. ORIGINAL REPORT: CALLER IS REPORTING A POTENTIAL SPILL OF MATERIALS AND RELEASE DUE TO A DERAILMENT ON THE MAIN LINE. CALLER STATED TWO LOCOMOTIVES AND FOUR TANKERS CAR WERE DERAILED. CALLER STATED TWO OF THE TANKER CARS ARE UPRIGHT BUT OFF THE TRACKS AND ARE EMPTY. CALLER STATED THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR A SPILL OF DIESEL. CALLER STATED THE TWO OTHER TANKER CARS HAVE RESIDUAL AMOUNTS OF ANHYDROUS AMMONIA INSIDE. CALLER STATED THE LOCOMOTIVE THAT DERAILED KNOCKED DOWN ACTIVE POWER POLES (1- 3 POLES). CALLER STATED THE SIX POWER LINES WERE OR MAYBE STILL ACROSS THE LOCOMOTIVES. CALLER STATED THE CREW WAS NOT ALLOWED TO LEAVE THE LOCOMOTIVES UNTIL THE POWER COMPANY CREW CAME ON THE SCENE TO ASSURE SAFETY TO EXIT THE TRAIN. CALLER STATED ONE CREW MEMBER WAS INJURED AND TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL. THE OTHER TWO CREW MEMBERS HAVE MINOR INJURIES BUT ARE GOING TO THE HOSPITAL TO GET CHECKED OUT. CALLER STATED THE DAMAGE AMOUNT IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME.

Report DescriptionNOAA/NESDIS MSPR: REPORT DATE: 06-12-2021 REPORT TIME: 0130 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: MAIN PASS 63 IMAGE DATE: 06-11-2021 IMAGE TIME: 1628 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL2B MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 10 METER LOCATION: 29°19"34" N/88°59"30" W AREA: 43.07 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH BOTH NRC #1307500 AND #1307478. THE FRAGMENTED ANOMALY AS A WHOLE WAS APPROXIMATELY 37.42 NMI IN LENGTH AND APPROX. 2.94 NMI AT ITS WIDEST. IT HAD HIGH CONTRAST AGAINST ITS SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT. RELATIVELY THICKER OIL WAS PRESENT DUE TO THE SHIMMER, METALLIC, AND WHITE PORTIONS VISIBLY SEEN ON IMAGERY. IT ALSO EXHIBITED A FEATHERING SIGNATURE THROUGHOUT ITS ENTIRETY. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE COMING FROM THE SW AT 11 KTS. WHICH ALIGNED WELL WITH THE ORIENTATION OF THE ANOMALY. UNCERTAINTIES: THE ANOMALY WAS FRAGMENTED DUE TO CLOUDS IN THE VICINITY. ALSO, BOTH NRC REPORTS MENTIONED ABOVE HAD TWO DIFFERENT LOCATIONS BUT IT WAS BELIEVED THAT THE ANOMALY MAY HAVE EMANATED FROM ONE SOURCE. THE POINT SOURCE WAS CHOSEN DUE TO THE MAJORITY OF THE RELATIVELY THICKER OIL LOCATED ON THE WESTERN END.

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BP EXPLORATION & PRODUCTION, INC

IT IS BELIEVED THAT SEVERAL DROPS OF THE HYDRAULIC FLUID ENTERED THE SEA.
